items.text: Cann-L, run by the City of Lausanne with Addiction Switzerland and funded by the city and the canton of Vaud, sells cannabis on a non-profit basis to enrolled participants through a specialised shop in Lausanne. Planned from July 2023 to June 2027, with up to 1,600 participants.

Under the federal pilot-trial rules, only adults who live in this canton and can show they already use cannabis may enrol. Participants may use the products only themselves: no passing them on and no use in publicly accessible places. Visitors from outside the canton can't enrol or buy, and the national cannabis ban applies to everyone outside the trials. Each trial is limited to five years, with one extension of up to two years possible; the legal basis for the trials ends on 14 May 2031.

Federal-approved cannabis pilot trial here: Cann-L (City of Lausanne): non-profit sale model. Pilot trials are scientific studies approved by the federal health office; organisers report to it yearly.

laws.rule: Since 1 October 2024, federal law has set a single minimum age of 18 across Switzerland for the sale of tobacco products and electronic cigarettes, including vending machines and online sales (Tobacco Products Act, art. 23). This canton follows that national rule. If staff are in doubt about a buyer's age, they should check it with an official photo identity document that shows a date of birth.
